title: Doorbell queueing and host-transfer latency survey
content:
Goal:
Quickly surface whether host->GPU doorbell/queueing effects and PCIe host transfer bursts are contributing to tail latency for small batched LLM inference (seq_len 32/64, batch 1-8) on our 8x A100 testbeds. We suspect host-side PCIe submission bursts and kernel launch serialization are amplifying NCCL microbursts and causing intermittent 2-3x latency outliers.

Context / why now:
- Recent user incident (ticket INF-2024-09-high-latency) showed 99.9p jumps correlated with increased upstream traffic.
- Existing microburst experiments looked at NCCL and packetization, but host-side submission patterns (doorbell/queue syscall timing) were not instrumented.
- Want pragmatic mitigations we can roll into request batching/driver config.

Testbed and topology:
- Nodes: 4x machines (SKU: rwd-x8-a100), each with 8x A100 40GB, Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 11.8, NVIDIA driver 535.54, NCCL 2.16.6, docker runtime runc, kernel 5.15.0-101.
- Interconnect: NVLink inside node, Mellanox InfiniBand HDR200 for cross-node. PCIe Gen4 x16 between CPU and GPU.
- Workloads: 1) tiny chat model (7B trimmed), 2) 70/30 mix of short and medium prompts to replicate PLG traffic.
- Serving runtime: local branch porta/doorbell-probe (PR linked above) with lightweight instrumentation for host submission timestamps and doorbell calls (via eBPF tracepoints + libbpf).

Measurement approach:
- Capture wallclock token time (start -> token_emit) at application layer.
- Capture host submission timeline: syscall write()/ioctl timings, queue pair doorbell events (via perf/eBPF), GPU kernel enqueue timestamps from NVidia CUPTI where available.
- Network traces for NCCL: nccl-tests microbench repeated and full-wave inference traces collected with tcpdump on IB interfaces.
- Two modes: unscheduled (baseline) and paced submission (user-level pacing introduced; inter-token submit sleep values 0 / 50us / 200us).
- Repeat each run 50 times; keep raw traces.

Quick reproduction commands (dev notes):
- start collector: sudo ./doorbell-collector --out /tmp/run1 --trace-pty
- run inference: ./run_inference.sh --model 7b-mini --seq 32 --batch 2 --requests 500
- convert traces: python tools/trace_align.py /tmp/run1/*.log --out /tmp/summary.json

Findings (high level):
1) Host submission bursts align with tail latency: Clear clusters where multiple submit calls occur within 3-10us windows and are followed 20-40us later by GPU kernel start delays (visible as large gaps in CUPTI enqueue->start). These clusters coincide with 99.5/99.9 latency spikes in the application-level token emission.
2) Pacing reduces 99.9p significantly: Adding a 50us gap between host submits reduced 99.9p by ~38% on average across nodes for batch sizes <=4. 200us gives similar but with higher median.
3) PCIe H2D transfer queues saturate intermittently when background I/O present: concurrent checkpoint copies (we ran background rsync) caused host DMA scheduling jitter and amplified doorbell crowding.
4) NCCL behaves differently per topology: within-node NVLink mitigates some stalls (shorter enqueue->start), but cross-node IB floods amplify waiting due to PCIe queue head-of-line in host.
5) Kernel launch serialization: observed driver-side serialization across small kernels (op granularity) — manifests as sequential kernel start times even when enqueue completed in close succession. Suspected path: CUDA driver serializing PTX kernels due to context locking or implicit stream synchronization in our runtime.

Representative numbers:
- Baseline (batch=2, seq=32): median token latency 35.2ms, 99p 78.6ms, 99.9p 210.1ms.
- With 50us pacing: median 36.0ms (slightly higher), 99p 62.3ms, 99.9p 130.2ms.
- With background rsync on host: 99.9p spikes exceeded 450ms intermittently.
- Within-node only runs saw 30% smaller enqueue->start gaps than cross-node runs on average.

Trace snippets (abbreviated):
- host_submit: t=1234567.345678 write(fd=23, size=4096) -> 0 (ret)
- eBPF doorbell: t=1234567.345685 doorbell(gpu0, q=5)
- CUPTI enqueue: t=1234567.345690 enqueue(kernel:matmul) stream 56
- CUPTI start: t=1234567.345732 kernel_start(matmul) -> delta 42us (gap)
- app_emit_token: t=1234567.345980 emit(token#12) -> delta from submit 305us

Root cause hypotheses (ranked):
A) Host submission bursts create PCIe DMA scheduling pressure -> driver queues + kernel launch serialization -> visible tail.
B) Driver-level stream/context locks cause implicit serialization of small kernels (we are enqueue-heavy with small matmuls).
C) NIC/IB interrupts and host CPU steal during IB flushes amplify queueing when cross-node traffic occurs.
D) Our runtime's batching algorithm emits bursts when multiple request futures resolve simultaneously (synchronous wakeups).

Mitigations tried (notes):
- User-space pacing (50us) – reliably reduces tail; cheap and immediately deployable as a runtime toggle.
- Coalesced DMA (combine small H2D transfers into single larger transfer) – reduced PCIe queue depth and improved 99p by ~12% in microbench, but required pinning and buffer consolidation changes in runtime.
- Stream affinity: bind critical kernels to dedicated CUDA streams to avoid implicit synchronization from using multiple default streams. Mixed results; helped when paired with coalescing.
- Background I/O throttling: simple cgroups for rsync prevented the pathological cases.

Open experiments / next steps:
- Re-run with CUDA 12.x driver (newer driver reported fixes around kernel launch parallelism).
- Iterate on user-space adaptive pacing: auto-measure enqueue->start gap and tune dynamic sleep; implement PID-ish controller so median unaffected while trimming tail.
- Validate on smaller GPU sizes (T4/RTX6000) since PCIe topology differs; important for Dedicated/edge plans.
- Confirm driver serialization by instrumenting cuLaunchKernel path via libcuda wrappers (todo: add LD_PRELOAD shim).
- Work with NVIDIA field engineer (have a support case) to get visibility into driver-side serialization and scheduled PCIe DMA behavior.

Action items (owners):
- Elena: ship adaptive submit pacing PoC to experiment branch (ETA 2 weeks)
- Marcus: run CUDA 12 test matrix on two nodes and report differences (ETA 10 days)
- Priya: add LD_PRELOAD kernel launch probe and collect 100-run traces (ETA 3 weeks)
- Owen: add coalesced H2D buffer mode behind feature flag and benchmark (ETA 4 weeks)
- Ops: throttle non-essential host IO on prod-sim nodes for next 48h (in-flight).

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Pacing trades median for tail; need to measure customer QoE impact for PLG traffic.
- Coalescing increases host memory pressure; may affect throughput under high concurrency.
- Driver-level fixes may be required; product-level mitigations are stopgaps.

Notes to reviewers:
- Raw traces are large; see linked_artifacts for PR with trace upload script.
- This doc is intentionally light on long-form background — it's an experiment log. Expect follow-up doc with consolidated numbers and recommended runtime defaults once PoC completes.
- If you have an internal NV support contact, ping me — driver visibility will materially shorten triage.

Slack references: #eng-serving-runtime (thread: doorbell-latency-2024-09), trace snippets posted in thread for quick scan.

Quick verdict (working hypothesis):
Host submission patterns (doorbell bursts) are a real source of tail latency in our micro-batch regime. Pragmatic runtime mitigations (pacing + coalesced H2D + stream affinity) reduce tail markedly; long-term fix likely needs driver/PCIe scheduling improvements or batching changes at higher level.
